\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{جنس} (jens)}{جنس (jens)}]{\fa{جنس} (jens) — material; goods, stock; a kind}

\label{lesson:FA-C459-jens}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a wholesaler, then the Persian for a retailer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{جنس}}
\textbf{\fa{جنس}} (\emph{jens}) — \textquotedblleft{}material; goods, stock; a kind\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{جنس} \fa{این} \fa{پیراهن} \fa{پنبه} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Jens-e in pirâhan panbe ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This shirt is made of cotton.
\end{quote}

Arabic plural \emph{ajnâs} 'goods'. \emph{Jens-e khub} — good-quality goods.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{jens} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{jins} 'kind, sort' (EtymDB). In Persian it came to mean the stuff a thing is made of, and goods for sale.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jens}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jens}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{jens}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a wholesaler, then the Persian for a retailer, then say \emph{jens} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{جنس} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Material; goods, stock; a kind\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کالا} (kâlâ)}{کالا (kâlâ)}]{\fa{کالا} (kâlâ) — goods, a product, a commodity}

\label{lesson:FA-C459-kala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a retailer, then the Persian for material.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کالا}}
\textbf{\fa{کالا}} (\emph{kâlâ}) — \textquotedblleft{}goods, a product, a commodity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کالاهای} \fa{این} \fa{فروشگاه} \fa{همه} \fa{خارجی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Kâlâ-hâ-ye in forushgâh hame khâreji ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The goods in this shop are all foreign.
\end{quote}

Formal; \emph{kâlâ-ye irâni} — goods made at home.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \emph{kâlâ} is not settled, and EtymDB does not list it. It is the usual word for goods in trade and in the news.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kâlâ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{kâlâ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a retailer, then the Persian for material, then say \emph{kâlâ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{کالا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Goods, a product, a commodity\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اصل} (asl)}{اصل (asl)}]{\fa{اصل} (asl) — genuine, original (of goods); the origin}

\label{lesson:FA-C459-asl}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for material, then the Persian for goods.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اصل}}
\textbf{\fa{اصل}} (\emph{asl}) — \textquotedblleft{}genuine, original (of goods); the origin\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{فرش} \fa{اصل} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In farsh asl ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This carpet is genuine.
\end{quote}

Arabic plural \emph{osul} 'principles'. \emph{Dar asl} — originally.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{asl} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{aṣl} 'origin, original' (EtymDB). Said of goods, it means the real thing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{asl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{asl}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for material, then the Persian for goods, then say \emph{asl} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تقلبی} (taqallobi)}{تقلبی (taqallobi)}]{\fa{تقلبی} (taqallobi) — fake, counterfeit}

\label{lesson:FA-C459-taqallobi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for goods, then the Persian for genuine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تقلبی}}
\textbf{\fa{تقلبی}} (\emph{taqallobi}) — \textquotedblleft{}fake, counterfeit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{ساعت} \fa{تقلبی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In sâ'at taqallobi ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This watch is a fake.
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{taqallob} 'cheating' + \emph{-i}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{taqallobi} is built from \emph{taqallob} 'cheating, fraud', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{taqallub} 'turning over', and the Persian ending \emph{-i}. EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taqallobi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{taqallobi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for goods, then the Persian for genuine, then say \emph{taqallobi} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گارانتی} (gârânti)}{گارانتی (gârânti)}]{\fa{گارانتی} (gârânti) — a guarantee, a warranty}

\label{lesson:FA-C459-garanti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for genuine, then the Persian for fake.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گارانتی}}
\textbf{\fa{گارانتی}} (\emph{gârânti}) — \textquotedblleft{}a guarantee, a warranty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{یخچال} \fa{دو} \fa{سال} \fa{گارانتی} \fa{دارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In yakhchâl do sâl gârânti dârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This fridge has a two-year guarantee.
\end{quote}

The formal word is \emph{zemânat}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gârânti} was borrowed from French and is usually traced to French \emph{garantie} 'guarantee'. EtymDB does not list the Persian word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gârânti}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gârânti}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{gârânti}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for genuine, then the Persian for fake, then say \emph{gârânti} again
\end{itemize}

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 452–459 — a review}

\label{lesson:FA-R459-review-452-459}



\begin{quote}
Say the Persian for a turn and to get an appointment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
